acceptance.gen10_is_comparison_not_truth: H=256 (~197K parameters) approximates the historical scale as a comparison point only

analysis.cost: train wall time, serialized bytes, inference throughput per width
analysis.marginal_gains: per rung, the paired-by-seed loss change vs the previous rung, per added parameter, with exact one-sided bounds
analysis.no_ranking: no pooled score; the curve and its marginal gains are the result
analysis.primary_curve: test_loss against exact parameter count and against presentations per parameter, with seed uncertainty at every rung
analysis.slices: phase and material slices at the knee and at H=512, computed from the exam FENs
analysis.thresholds: first useful rung (best loss below the H=1 rung with bounds excluding zero), the knee (the rung with the largest marginal gain), the diminishing-return region (marginal gains whose bounds include zero), and every non-monotonic step
analysis.undertraining_test: for H=128/256/512: control vs primary at the same width, paired by seed; a control rung that recovers the knee's loss indicates undertraining, one that does not indicates capacity saturation (within the 4x envelope)

control_rule.anchor: H=128 is the smallest control width, so the report can see whether extra compute merely rescues the largest models or moves the curve more generally
control_rule.limitation_stated_up_front: if 4x does not rescue a width, the evidence distinguishes 'capacity saturated' from 'compute helped less than 4x', NOT from 'no amount of compute helps'
control_rule.rule: one constant multiplier, 4x, identical for all three control widths; no per-width tuning, no tuning after outcomes
control_rule.why_not_proportional_to_parameters: updates proportional to parameter count would multiply H=512's run time by ~128 (days); a constant factor is the largest predeclared multiplier that keeps the control arm inside a few hours
